characters.name: Marrow Reedfold
characters.role: Guardian of Hall of Three Records

dialogue.speaker: temple.1.agent
dialogue.text: I bought my stall board one letter at a time. Today I could afford the Y in my name.

options.text: Invite Mabry Brassey to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.1.agent
dialogue.text: Gold scatters cold light across the wall. No writing appears underneath it. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.1.guardian
dialogue.text: I can give light a weight, almost. I cannot weigh what it cost the boy to ask for his coin back.

options.text: Hold the lamp for Mabry while she shows the buyer
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.1.guardian
dialogue.text: Mabry turns the bowl herself. For once the person who sold the story has to stand in its light.

dialogue.speaker: temple.2.agent
dialogue.text: My father reads our case to visitors. I wanted him to get through a day without anyone laughing.

options.text: Invite Wystan Greer to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.2.agent
dialogue.text: Its last mark trails off the edge. The copyist never saw the end of the older roll. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.2.guardian
dialogue.text: I used to give the oldest reed the highest hook. Rain gets to the oldest reed first, too.

options.text: Leave the later slip on Marrow’s high hook
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.2.guardian
dialogue.text: Wystan’s father can find the correction without a younger hand turning the roll for him.

dialogue.speaker: temple.3.agent
dialogue.text: My little sister practised our name every night. She thought it would fit if she wrote small enough.

options.text: Invite Osric Coldry to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.3.agent
dialogue.text: The blank has four square corners. A slip was lifted out after the page was numbered. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.3.guardian
dialogue.text: Nobody told me how long a seed can sleep. I am still waiting for one my sister planted.

options.text: Let the family lift the pane themselves
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.3.guardian
dialogue.text: Odile sets a tea towel across the envelope. Mossgrave warms one corner for her alone.

dialogue.speaker: temple.4.agent
dialogue.text: They used to ask my teacher what I had said while I stood beside him.

options.text: Invite Astor Quaile to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.4.agent
dialogue.text: The near berth dries before the slower boat can turn. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.4.guardian
dialogue.text: I once told a child every height the water might reach. She was asking where to leave her shoes.

options.text: Set a peg where the child can leave her shoes
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.4.guardian
dialogue.text: Astor makes a safe shelf for today. Tomorrow’s tide keeps both its shadows.

dialogue.speaker: temple.5.agent
dialogue.text: If my numbers look soft, they will cut down my listening post. My brother built it high enough for me.

options.text: Invite Gale Pryce to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.5.agent
dialogue.text: One bird casts two shadows across the forked lamp. The moths count themselves until somebody laughs. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.5.guardian
dialogue.text: We counted my sister twice. It felt like having her back. Please keep the two numbers where we can see them.

options.text: Give the dawn watcher a second slate
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.5.guardian
dialogue.text: Gale opens a line for a reply heard off the edge of the first count. The two watchers will meet at dusk.

dialogue.speaker: temple.6.agent
dialogue.text: I could get her method into the guild book. I could not get her through its front door.

options.text: Invite Harl Tagg to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.6.agent
dialogue.text: Changing just the cooling bath leaves a bend in only one slip. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.6.guardian
dialogue.text: My elbow rings false when it is cold. I once failed a perfectly good hammer before breakfast.

options.text: Put Grisel’s cold and warm strikes on the docket
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.6.guardian
dialogue.text: The guild copies two conditions onto its label. Harl sets a stool at the bench for the traveller.

dialogue.speaker: temple.7.agent
dialogue.text: If the press sleeps tonight, three families go without a shift tomorrow.

options.text: Invite Liesl Marrable to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.7.agent
dialogue.text: A shop nick repeats on both copies. The nick places the shop but cannot tell the twins apart. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.7.guardian
dialogue.text: I remember spilling the coffee. So does my brother. Would you turn the paper over for us?

options.text: Keep the two corrections facing each other
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.7.guardian
dialogue.text: The twins give one another the clean sides to sign. Liesl hangs both at the public press.

dialogue.speaker: temple.8.agent
dialogue.text: When our boat radio failed I could say only one name clearly. I wanted one word every crew could hear.

options.text: Invite Penrose Abernathy to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.8.agent
dialogue.text: It clears the shoal on a falling tide. The far bank shares its printed name with the landing. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.8.guardian
dialogue.text: The first printed chart I ever saw had my sister’s reef on it. Somebody must have listened.

options.text: Leave space for the surveyor and the singer to sign
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.8.guardian
dialogue.text: Penrose reads each name back to its speaker. The two people disagree about where the reef ends.

dialogue.speaker: temple.9.agent
dialogue.text: An empty house sounds like somebody drawing a very long breath and never letting it go.

options.text: Invite Lucan Fairweather to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.9.agent
dialogue.text: A crate hides the actor’s hand from the balcony. The first row saw a wave. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.9.guardian
dialogue.text: I watched from the wings for thirty years before anyone offered me a seat. Which chair did they keep for you?

options.text: Trade the prompt mask for the last spectator’s ticket
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.9.guardian
dialogue.text: Lucan sits in the seat he used to describe to other people. He crosses a word off the programme.

dialogue.speaker: temple.10.agent
dialogue.text: My mother taught me to keep the coins for flour apart from the coins for someone worse off. This week both jars are empty.

options.text: Invite Cass Mott to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.10.agent
dialogue.text: Its double base weighs as much as a handful of grain. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.10.guardian
dialogue.text: My left hand and my right agree to a grain. They have never had to buy a loaf.

options.text: Hand the check basket to the customer
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.10.guardian
dialogue.text: Cass waits while a child steadies the brass hands. The queue watches the wicker tip the empty pan.

dialogue.speaker: temple.11.agent
dialogue.text: My sister and I used to sing across the weir. After the last public meeting she stopped answering.

options.text: Invite Dorran Sluys to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.11.agent
dialogue.text: The lower cup is short. Water soaks into the dry bank on its way down. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.11.guardian
dialogue.text: Lull fell asleep at the meeting. Brisk called it agreement. Swirl kept his cup upside down till morning.

options.text: Let the smallest crew sound the next turn
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.11.guardian
dialogue.text: The upstream crew hears its own gate discussed from downstream. Dorran leaves both meeting dates posted.

dialogue.speaker: temple.12.agent
dialogue.text: Our street is quiet for the first time in years. I forgot quiet could sound exactly like being left out.

options.text: Invite Nyle Ostry to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.12.agent
dialogue.text: The household goes west on the list and waits for a cart that never comes. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.12.guardian
dialogue.text: I can show every turn of my wheels. I still need a person to tell me whose house this is.

options.text: Walk the missed doorstep with its resident
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.12.guardian
dialogue.text: Nyle pencils in both entrances and initials the route change. The library arrives from the quieter street.

dialogue.speaker: temple.13.agent
dialogue.text: I hid my own family’s page first. After that, every empty space looked like a little kindness.

options.text: Invite Tolly Fadden to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.13.agent
dialogue.text: A second cane answers the first. The walker had company for this part. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.13.guardian
dialogue.text: I know that pause. I cannot tell you whose it is until they say I may.

options.text: Let the family choose the public pause
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.13.guardian
dialogue.text: Tolly keeps the private voice with the family. Visitors can still find the point at which the public take ends.

dialogue.speaker: temple.14.agent
dialogue.text: People remember my face after a lecture. I wish somebody remembered the question I brought with me.

options.text: Invite Sabine Orrell to stand beside the trial.
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.14.agent
dialogue.text: The low field keeps a crop. The higher bed dries before the fair. I will put my name beside that.

dialogue.speaker: temple.14.guardian
dialogue.text: I was going to put the blue ribbon on that row. My mother says the smallest tree is the only one that looks like home.

options.text: Leave the shade cloth in the gardener’s hands
Leave room for another witness.

dialogue.speaker: temple.14.guardian
dialogue.text: Sabine helps the gardener lift the cloth. Visitors can run either season and read who planted each row.

missions.title: Lantern Undercroft
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What can a pattern on the surface tell us about how something was made, and what can it not tell us?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Lantern Undercroft and take up Lamplight.

missions.title: Hall of Three Records
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How do we share a record without handing on more certainty than it can support?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Hall of Three Records and take up Trace Thread.

missions.title: Frost Vault
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can a public record name what it knows and still leave room for a missing link?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Frost Vault and take up Keeping Frost.

missions.title: Tide Dome
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When should a change in evidence change what we tell other people?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Tide Dome and take up Weather Eye.

missions.title: Root Hall
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What changes when we watch the same place from another position or listen to someone who works there?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Root Hall and take up Many Eyes.

missions.title: Quench Forge
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How far can a material test support a story about where two things came from?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Quench Forge and take up True Temper.

missions.title: Press of Echoes
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What does a claim become when it travels without its limits or its source?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Press of Echoes and take up Original Sight.

missions.title: Blank Lighthouse
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What can a map’s empty spaces lead people to assume?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Blank Lighthouse and take up Blank Chart.

missions.title: Dark Stage
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How does the timing of an action shape the reason an audience sees in it?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Dark Stage and take up Stage Whisper.

missions.title: Balance Hall
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What must we hold alike to make a comparison that someone else can use?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Balance Hall and take up Fair Weight.

missions.title: Spring Steps
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can a shared rule stay fair when a measurement and the conditions change?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Spring Steps and take up Common Current.

missions.title: Clockwork Hall
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How do the people we count and the rules we use shape the service others can reach?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Clockwork Hall and take up Open Gears.

missions.title: Listening Well
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can a public sign carry a local account and help someone who arrives by another path?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Listening Well and take up Second Ear.

missions.title: Model Garden
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When does a change at one landing make the original route plan too narrow?

objectives.title: Settle the case at Model Garden and take up Small World.

hints.text: A boy holds a gold stamp under the dead lamp. Mabry quietly puts the refund money back inside her sleeve.
Try the instrument to the left. Turn the stamped face to the wick.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Slide the stallholder’s dated receipt into the lamp.
Bring both readings to Brannoc the Lampwright at the centre. Hang the receipt where buyers can lift it or choose another settlement.
Marrow catches a loose reed in the door. Someone has rubbed a date from the paper where the fold hid it.
Try the instrument to the left. Unroll the storekeeper’s copy.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Hold the later delivery slip against the gap.
Bring both readings to Marrow Reedfold at the centre. Leave both rolls on separate pins or choose another settlement.
A warm thumbprint blooms over a blank name in the ice. Mossgrave tries to close the lid on Odile’s hand.
Try the instrument to the left. Catch the impression on the cold pane.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Warm the flap with the family seal.
Bring both readings to Mossgrave at the centre. Mark the missing slip on the public file or choose another settlement.
Halcy’s tide globe spills a second blue shadow across the harbour plan. Astor has painted only one line on the bell card.
Try the instrument to the left. Advance the tide wheel a notch.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Draw the wind vane across the same hour.
Bring both readings to Halcy Brightwater at the centre. Call the earliest safe tide by bell or choose another settlement.
Ninefold lands on the tally board in the shape of a question mark. Gale’s neat last column has no space for a call without a sighting.
Try the instrument to the left. Count shadows at dusk.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Turn the screen to the dawn reeds.
Bring both readings to Ninefold at the centre. Add a column for heard-only calls or choose another settlement.
A hot sample rolls under Grisel’s boot. Harl’s form lists a guild recipe. The smith who taught it worked outside the gate.
Try the instrument to the left. Quench twin slips with the same weight.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Repeat the cool bath in a different clamp.
Bring both readings to Grisel Anvilsong at the centre. Leave room for the traveller’s account in the register or choose another settlement.
The twin printers catch opposite ends of a falling proof. Each recognises their own coffee ring. Liesl has already sold the next edition.
Try the instrument to the left. Match the torn edge to the first forme.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Overlay the forgotten author’s correction.
Bring both readings to Mirro and Orrim at the centre. Print the correction on the next run or choose another settlement.
Old Saltmark sings a name beyond the edge of Penrose’s survey. An apprentice has already tied a mooring rope to the wrong blue peg.
Try the instrument to the left. Steer by the printed sounding.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Steer by the pilot’s sung turn.
Bring both readings to Old Saltmark at the centre. Mark both names with the depth and date or choose another settlement.
Lucan hands out a programme headed REFUSAL. From the last seat the empty chair looks like a deliberate insult.
Try the instrument to the left. Move the mask from prompt corner to balcony.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Light the aisle behind the empty chair.
Bring both readings to The Prompter at the centre. Let the ushers print both sightlines or choose another settlement.
Quarta sets three baskets on the brass hands. Cass puts a seal over the place where the wicker weight should go.
Try the instrument to the left. Weigh the empty nesting basket.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Swap wicker while keeping the grain.
Bring both readings to Dame Quarta Evenhand at the centre. Settle today’s sale by the tare or choose another settlement.
Brisk carries three cups through the spring and brings back two full. Dorran’s upstream and downstream crews signed on different days.
Try the instrument to the left. Split one turn equally at the head gate.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Let the last crew call the gate change.
Bring both readings to Lull, Brisk and Swirl at the centre. Bring both crews to the wet bank or choose another settlement.
Ledgerlock lifts a brass foot over the district line and stalls. Nyle’s rule has no square for a doorstep shared by two streets.
Try the instrument to the left. Run the rule from the east entrance.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Move the starting peg to the west entrance.
Bring both readings to Ledgerlock at the centre. Keep both route names and one shared stop or choose another settlement.
Hollin lifts a hand at a footstep nobody else picked out. Tolly has clipped a family voice to the public copy of a walk.
Try the instrument to the left. Listen from the bridge stair.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Follow the listener’s access slip.
Bring both readings to Hollin Softvoice at the centre. Keep the voice in the family room or choose another settlement.
Tansy fits the last paper tree into the garden. Sabine brings a ribbon from a famous visitor. The model harvest fails on the shaded side.
Try the instrument to the left. Run the dry slope with the same rain.
Cross to the instrument on the right. Add the narrow shade cloth and rerun.
Bring both readings to Tansy Littlemore at the centre. Invite the gardener to demonstrate the shade or choose another settlement.
